$comment: Strings that were corrected on a live surface and must not come back.
This exists because corrected copy has a way of returning. Design plates, drafts and audits are
written against whatever the site said on the day they were made, and porting one months later
silently reinstates every claim fixed since - inside work that is otherwise wanted, which is
exactly when nobody re-reads the sentences.
Each entry names the string, why it was wrong, and the day the correction shipped, so a reader
who trips this can read the reasoning rather than guess at it. Matching is whitespace- and
apostrophe-normalised, because JSX splits a sentence across lines and prettier moves the break.
Adding copy that trips a rule here is not a reason to delete the rule. It is a reason to check
whether the claim became true - and if it did, to say so in the entry and remove it deliberately.

patterns: pool's whole staking yield goes to one depositor
whole pool's interest goes to one depositor
prize is funded entirely from the staking yield
Prizes are funded from realised staking yield
Prizes are funded solely from pooled staking yield
prizes come from the pooled staking yield
rules.why: The mechanism is real but it is not what has paid. The harvester has not yet covered a prize and sponsors have funded every draw settled so far. Stating the mechanism as history is the one thing the site's own 'verify it yourself' invitation cannot survive.
rules.instead: Describe the design, then say what has actually funded the draws, next to the figures.

rules.why: SuiNS charges $10 for the first year and $5 to renew, read from getPriceList() and getRenewalPriceList() on mainnet. '$10 a year' overstates the ongoing cost and contradicted the price table four sections below it on the same page.
rules.instead: State the first-year and renewal figures separately, as the registrar charges them.

patterns: Your competition. Your licence. Our draw.
rules.why: Operator correction: the draw is not ours, it is Sui mainnet's. The organiser holds the licence, the prize and the customer; the chain settles the draw.
rules.instead: Your competition. Your licence. Sui Mainnet Draw.

rules.why: SuiNS pricing is DAO-mutable on-chain config. A figure typed into a component is a mirror nobody checks, and stale here means quoting a price the registrar will not honour.
rules.instead: Read the price from chain state, or name the registrar's published schedule with a date.

patterns: describes how the prize is funded — from yield rather than
rules.why: No loss follows from principal never being spent, whatever funds the prize. Explaining it by funding source tied the guarantee to a fact that is currently false.
rules.instead: 'No loss' describes what happens to your principal - it is never spent, whatever funds the prize.

patterns: start at fifteen to forty-five thousand dollars
below that line there has been nothing
the layer below the audit shouldn't be empty
rules.why: Two unsupportable claims in one sentence on a page that asks to be checked. Of eighteen firms serving Sui, exactly one publishes a price and it starts near seven thousand for a standard review - so a fifteen-thousand floor is falsifiable by any reader who has asked for a quote. And the layer below is not empty: open-source Move mutation testing exists, is actively maintained, and one engine is Sui-only and already ships as a pull-request action.
rules.instead: Quote the only published audit prices there are, and claim the difference that survives a hostile reader: the existing tools leave an exit code and a console log, and nobody produces a shareable, attestable, per-commit assurance artifact for Move.

rules.why: Purged hosts. The DNS record was deleted and the Vercel project removed on 8 August 2026, so neither name resolves and any link to one is dead. Serving a retirement page would first require re-attaching the domain, which has not been done.
rules.instead: Nothing. The card does not render.

rules.why: The live protocol charges 2.9% of ticket sales - quoted as 'the whole fee' on protocolx.io and locked into each competition at creation. '0.5% of prize, min $10' understated the fee 5.8x and described a pricing shape (percent of prize with a dollar floor) that the contract does not implement.
rules.instead: 2.9% of ticket sales, the whole fee, locked at creation - matching what protocolx.io quotes and what the contract charges.

patterns: Every thirty minutes it wakes for one beat
rules.why: The beat has been paused since 2026-10-04; the newest post on Heron's public record is dated that day. Present-tense cadence copy on a silent agent is exactly the kind of claim the site's verify-it-yourself invitation invites a reader to falsify.
rules.instead: Past tense with the pause named and dated: it woke every thirty minutes; the beat has been paused since 2026-10-04.

rules.why: The gateway repository was renamed to xlaunch-gateway, and the product's LICENSE is proprietary ('no licence is granted'), not BUSL-1.1. The old org path 404s and the licence card mislabelled the source.
rules.instead: Nothing on this site, for now. The gateway is proprietary infrastructure; it gets a card only when a public, licensed artifact exists, and that card names xlaunch-gateway and the real licence.

rules.why: Four org paths that 404: move-mutate, digest-guard and drift-watch are private components inside the protocolx-verify repository, never published as repos, and the old scripts/reproduce.sh clone path pointed at an org repo that does not exist. 'Runnable today' copy linking to dead repos is the one defect this site's pitch cannot survive.
rules.instead: Link what exists - the published protocolx-verify repository - and describe the rest as part of it, not as standalone repos.

rules.why: The product's own README publishes $149 / repository / month for the hosted App. This site printed a list price the product does not charge, and the two surfaces contradicted each other on the same day.
rules.instead: $149 / repo / month, matching the product README.

rules.why: /verify served an HTML page, so the piped command fed markup to a shell - and piping any remote script straight into sh executes code nobody has inspected. The product installs as a GitHub Action, which is a reviewed, pinned artifact.
rules.instead: The workflow step: uses: Northlatch-Labs-LLC/protocolx-verify@v1, or /install.sh to scaffold the workflow file into a repo.
